prompt_fit_bound.basis: NOT MEASURED IN THIS REGISTRATION. core.flight.cli check's _assess_prompt_budget is the measurement and it runs in the coordinator's own clean-tree re-pin cycle on the minted receipt; the registration agent did not run it. What IS measured here, model-free from the released authored document, is the WORST-CASE SUPPLIED CHARACTERS per node at the unchanged caps 4 / 8 / 4 / 4: perception 528, solver 1,035, reviewer 471, planner 479, against v1r's 485 / 938 / 423 / 381 and v2's 476 / 850 / 416 / 269, with the longest single statement at 140 characters (126 at v1r and v2) and the mean at 88.9. The token bound is therefore expected to be CELL-2's measured one plus those character deltas, roughly +15 / +53 / +16 / +60 tokens at about 3.5 characters per token -- an ESTIMATE, stated so that a surprise in the coordinator's check is visible as a surprise.
prompt_fit_bound.decision: EXPECTED ALLOW on perception, reviewer and planner and EXPECTED COMPACT_REQUIRED on the SOLVER phase, whose worst case already exceeded the live slot less its one-eighth reserve (24,576 - 3,072) by 317 tokens at CELL-2's smaller store and grows by roughly 53 more here. That is a BOUND, not a prediction: it assumes every supplied store renders its cap at its longest on one row. The episode declares context_fit_policy 'compact-or-abstain', so a Solver request that really does exceed the window is COMPACTED, never truncated, and every compaction is counted in the E20 receipts. If the coordinator's check reports a BLOCKER rather than COMPACT_REQUIRED, the cell does not open and the caps are the thing to reconsider -- not the reserve.

supply_reach.what_it_means: Every value of the released store is reachable by a registered candidate intent on every node, arm and twin -- 448 of 448 -- so no route is inert by construction and none is removed from the fragment (the B9a-rec rule). 38 of the 60 registered SLURP candidate intents are covered. What the GEPA release CHANGES against v1r is how often a candidate-bound route finds a match and fills its cap: the Planner slice grows from 14 values over 4 intents to 77 over 33, and CELL-1 measured that route at 0.594 of rows supplied, 1.259 items per supplied row and never at cap. The four-row smoke measures the realised per-node counts before the arm opens (all three candidate-bound routes reach cap on three of its four rows), and the verdict reports the Planner route separately rather than pooled.

cell1_measured_consumption_for_compariso.what_to_expect: an UPPER bound on nothing and a LOWER bound on nothing: the GEPA store is larger and reaches more intents at every node, so rows supplied, items per supplied row and rows at cap are all expected to rise, most of all at the Planner. The realised numbers are measured on the flight.

revisit_supply_rule: REGISTERED BEFORE CONTACT, and a correction of the rule CELL-2's driver carried: at a 448-value store a REVISE revisit acquires a SECOND, DISJOINT slice at each revisited node, because a candidate-bound route excludes what the accumulated QueryState already holds and then fills its cap from what is left. The offline dry run measures arm Solver 1 / Reviewer 4 / Planner 4 and twin Solver 4 / Reviewer 4 / Planner 0 on the second visit, with 25 (arm) and 24 (twin) distinct delta value ids over the episode and ZERO duplicate acquisitions. The invariant this cell registers is DISJOINTNESS, not emptiness: QueryState refuses a duplicate retrieved_value_id, EvidenceAgentController._acquired_ids refuses such a decision and the trajectory dies (the 2026-09-17 cell B1 abort). At CELL-2's 200-value store there was no second slice to find, so the two rules could not be told apart there. The consequence is a cost, not a defect: a revised row carries more delta text, which the E20 compaction count and the frontier row's token basis both report.
